skill.description: Deprecated MCP server building guide for mcp-use. It explains tools, resources, prompts, resource templates, response helpers, and React widgets. New work should use mcp-app-builder.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, TypeScript template literals, environment variable examples, and localhost URLs. One real issue remains: the deprecated skill asks users to run an npx installer for a replacement skill. No prompt injection text or credential exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Installer command in deprecated skill description
remediation.suggestion: Remove the npx command from metadata. Link to marketplace installation guidance that requires explicit human confirmation.

remediation.issue: API key shown in URL query example
remediation.suggestion: Prefer examples that send API keys through headers when the upstream service supports it.

remediation.issue: Environment variable examples lack safety notes
remediation.suggestion: Add a short reminder to use empty .env.example values and never commit real secrets.

content.value_statement: MCP developers need consistent patterns for tools, resources, prompts, and widgets. This skill summarizes mcp-use implementation patterns and warns that new work should use mcp-app-builder.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of mcp-use server tools with Zod schemas and response helpers.
Explains read-only resources, parameterized resource templates, and reusable prompts.
Shows how widgets connect server tool outputs to React TSX UI files.
Documents response helper choices for text, object, markdown, HTML, media, binary, errors, and widgets.
Provides evaluation examples for common MCP implementation tasks.
Identifies that the skill is deprecated and points to mcp-app-builder.
limitations: The skill is deprecated, so active users should prefer mcp-app-builder.
It is documentation-only and does not generate a complete project without agent file edits.
Examples use placeholder APIs and require adaptation for real services.
Some examples mention package installation and external APIs that need human approval.

use_cases.title: Create MCP Tools
use_cases.description: Design tool schemas, response helpers, and error handling for mcp-use servers.

use_cases.title: Model Read-Only Data
use_cases.description: Define resources and resource templates for configuration, profiles, and other structured data.

use_cases.title: Add Interactive Widgets
use_cases.description: Connect server-side MCP tools to React TSX widget files and visible tool output.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a basic mcp-use tool for this task: [task]. Include schema fields, descriptions, response helper choice, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Add Resources and Prompts
prompt_templates.prompt: Design MCP resources and prompts for this server: [server goal]. Separate read-only data from actions and explain each URI pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Widget Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a widget-backed MCP workflow for [user workflow]. Include tool names, widget props, model-visible output, and loading states.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this mcp-use server plan for production readiness. Check schemas, destructive actions, environment variables, widgets, and deployment assumptions.

output_examples.input: Build a weather tool with a widget.
output_examples.output: A short implementation plan with the tool schema, widget name, response helper, and environment variable setup.
A resource design with a parameterized URI, user identifier validation, structured profile data, and not-found handling.
A prompt template specification with described fields, completion guidance, and response helper selection.

best_practices: Prefer mcp-app-builder for new work because this skill is deprecated.
Require explicit approval before running package-manager install commands.
Document required environment variables with empty examples, not real credentials.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real API keys into examples or generated files.
Do not treat destructive actions as read-only MCP tools.
Do not expose widget props to the model when private data is only for UI.

faq.question: Is this skill current?
faq.answer: No. It is deprecated and directs new users to mcp-app-builder.

faq.question: What framework does it target?
faq.answer: It targets MCP servers built with the mcp-use framework.

faq.question: Can it help build widgets?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains React TSX widgets, widget metadata, tool output, and the useWidget hook.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It contains an npx install instruction that should require human approval before use.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: It lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use environment variables and .env.example files with empty values. Never store real secrets in generated projects.
